headline: Loans and margin grow but earnings dip as fee revenue falls
summary_short: BOK Financial earned $159.9M, or $2.64 per diluted share, in Q3 2026 versus $2.92 last quarter; net interest income rose $18.1M to $370.0M and margin widened to 3.00%.
summary_long: Period-end loans grew $646M to $27.7B, led by energy, industrial-facility and mortgage-finance loans, and were up 11.5% y/y. Fees and commissions fell to $188.0M from $202.0M as brokerage and trading revenue dropped $13.0M. Operating expense was steady at $360.7M. Nonperforming assets were $67M, or 0.24% of loans, and net charge-offs were $886 thousand. Deposits slipped $324M to $39.5B. Common equity tier 1 was 12.73% and tangible common equity 9.16%.
confidence_notes: Release compares to the prior quarter. Prior-quarter net income of $176.5M included a Visa B share exchange gain and an AFS repositioning loss; excluding them it would have been $156.5M, or $2.59 per share. The shard's period labels differ from the release's quarter; the release's Q3 2026 columns are used.

drivers.explanation: Net interest income and margin benefited from loan growth and fixed-rate asset repricing.
A nearly 80 bp rise in the 10-year Treasury yield cut customer demand for fixed-income and mortgage products, lowering brokerage, trading and mortgage banking revenue.
Other operating revenue fell $46.1M q/q as the prior quarter included a net gain on the exchange of Visa B shares.
Growth was led by energy loans, loans secured by industrial facilities and mortgage finance loans.
